records.source: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
records.gloss: After now the to have ceased the uproar having sent for the Paul the disciples and having encouraged [them], having said farewell he went out to go to Macedonia.
pieces: When the uproar had died down, Paul sent for the disciples and encouraged them. Then he said goodbye and set out for Macedonia.

L.1: Now after the uproar had ceased, Paul, having sent for the disciples and encouraged [them], said farewell and departed to go to Macedonia.

R.1: After the riot in Ephesus was over, Paul called the followers of Jesus together and encouraged them. Then he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

decisions.choice: the uproar: the riot in the theater at Ephesus
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the riot in 19:23-41 (19:23 calls it a great disturbance). Paul had already planned to go through Macedonia (19:21).

decisions.choice: encouraged: urged and strengthened them
decisions.reason: The verb covers urging, encouraging and comforting. Here, at a parting, it means strengthening them to go on (as in 14:22, 16:40).

decisions.choice: the riot in Ephesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the event, which the reader met in chapter 19.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the disciples are.

records.heading: Through Macedonia and Greece

records.source: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς· γενομένης ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας.
records.gloss: Having gone through then the regions those and having encouraged them with word much he came into the Greece, \v 3 having spent and months three, having been made a plot against him by the Jews being about to set sail into the Syria, there came [to be] a decision of the to return through Macedonia.
pieces: He went through those parts, speaking at length to the disciples to encourage them, and came to Greece.
He stayed there three months. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews laid a plot against him, so he made up his mind to go back through Macedonia.

L.2: And having gone through those regions and encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece;
L.3: and having spent three months [there], when a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he resolved to return through Macedonia.

R.2: He went through that area and spoke many times to the believers there to make them strong. Then he went to Greece.
R.3: He stayed there for three months. He was getting ready to sail to Syria, but he learned that some of the Jews had made a plan to attack him. So he decided to go back the way he had come, through Macedonia.

decisions.choice: Greece: southern Greece, the Roman province of Achaia, where Corinth lay
decisions.reason: Macedonia was the northern province. Paul had worked in Achaia before (18:1, 18:12, 18:27).

decisions.choice: a plot by the Jews: a plan to harm him, timed to his sailing
decisions.reason: The word means a secret plan against someone (9:24, 23:30). Luke ties it to the voyage, and the plot makes Paul change his route.

decisions.choice: there came to be a decision: he made up his mind
decisions.reason: The phrase means that a resolve was formed. Paul is the one who changes plan.

decisions.choice: the disciples / the believers there
decisions.reason: "Them" means the disciples in those regions; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: he learned that; the way he had come
decisions.reason: Readable adds that Paul found out about the plot and that Macedonia was the road he had come by (20:1). Both follow from the story.

records.source: συνείπετο δὲ αὐτῷ Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος, καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος, Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος·
records.gloss: Accompanied then him Sopater of Pyrrhus a Berean, of Thessalonians and Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius a Derbean and Timothy, Asians and Tychicus and Trophimus.
pieces: He was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

L.4: And Sopater [son] of Pyrrhus, a Berean, accompanied him, and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and [men] of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

R.4: Several men traveled with Paul. They were Sopater son of Pyrrhus, from the city of Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus, from Thessalonica; Gaius, from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus, from the province of Asia.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "Sopater of Pyrrhus", with no "as far as Asia"
alternatives: many later manuscripts leave out "of Pyrrhus"
many manuscripts add "as far as Asia" after "accompanied him"
decisions.reason: The name of Sopater's father is in the early manuscripts and missing from many later ones. Many manuscripts also say these men went with Paul "as far as Asia", which does not fit 20:5-6 well. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: men from the churches Paul had founded, traveling with him to Jerusalem
alternatives: a group with no stated purpose
decisions.reason: Paul's letters speak of a gift for the poor in Jerusalem gathered from the churches of Macedonia, Achaia and Galatia, to be taken by men the churches chose (Romans 15:25-26; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4; 2 Corinthians 8:19-23). In 24:17 Paul says he came bringing gifts. Luke does not say here that these men carried it.

decisions.choice: Gaius of Derbe: another Gaius than the Macedonian of 19:29
decisions.reason: Gaius was a common name. This one is from Derbe in Galatia (14:20).

decisions.choice: Several men traveled with Paul.
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the list with a short sentence of its own.

records.source: οὗτοι δὲ προσελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι·
records.gloss: These and having gone ahead were waiting for us in Troas.
pieces: These men went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.

L.5: And these, having gone ahead, were waiting for us in Troas.

R.5: They went on ahead of us and waited for us in the city of Troas.

decisions.choice: us: the narrator includes himself in the group
alternatives: the narrator copies someone else's account
decisions.reason: The first person plural was last used at Philippi (16:10-17). It returns here, as Paul passes through Philippi again (20:6), and runs to 21:18. The text does not say who the narrator is.

decisions.choice: these: probably the whole group of 20:4
alternatives: only Tychicus and Trophimus, the last named
decisions.reason: "These" could point back to the last two names, but most naturally takes in the whole list.

decisions.choice: the city of Troas
decisions.reason: Readable says what Troas is, as at 16:8.

records.source: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων, καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε, οὗ διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά.
records.gloss: We then sailed away after the days of the Unleavened [Bread] from Philippi and came to them at Troas within days five, where we stayed days seven.
pieces: We ourselves sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and five days later we joined them at Troas. We spent seven days there.

L.6: But we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.

R.6: We sailed from Philippi after the Jewish Festival of Unleavened Bread. Five days later we met the others in Troas, and we stayed there for a week.

decisions.choice: the days of Unleavened Bread: the seven-day festival that followed Passover
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:15-20 and Luke 22:1. Luke dates the journey by the Jewish calendar; Pentecost (20:16) came seven weeks after Passover.

decisions.choice: within five days: the crossing took five days
alternatives: they arrived on the fifth day of the festival
decisions.reason: The same crossing the other way took two days (16:11); this one was slower.

decisions.choice: the Jewish Festival of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of days these were.

decisions.choice: a week
decisions.reason: Plainer English for the same length of time.

records.source: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον, παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου.
records.gloss: On then the first of the week, having been gathered together we to break bread, the Paul was discussing with them, being about to depart on the next day, he prolonged and the word until midnight.
pieces: On the first day of the week we met together to break bread. Paul spoke with the people there, because he intended to leave the next day, and his talk went on until midnight.

L.7: And on the first [day] of the week, when we had gathered to break bread, Paul was talking with them, since he was about to depart the next day, and he prolonged [his] message until midnight.

R.7: On the first day of the week, we met together to break bread and share the Lord's meal. Paul was planning to leave the next day, so he talked with the believers for a long time. He kept talking until midnight.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: the day after the Sabbath, the day Jesus rose
decisions.reason: Luke 24:1 uses the same phrase. If the day was counted from sunset, as Jews counted it, the meeting was on what is now Saturday evening; if from midnight or dawn, on Sunday evening. The text does not settle it. See also 1 Corinthians 16:2.

decisions.choice: to break bread: a shared meal that included the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: "Breaking bread" is used of the believers' meals together (2:42, 2:46) and of Jesus's meals (Luke 22:19, 24:30, 24:35). Paul calls the cup and the bread a sharing in Christ (1 Corinthians 10:16; 11:20-26). Here the gathering is for this purpose.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "we" had gathered
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "the disciples" had gathered
decisions.reason: The early manuscripts keep the first person here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was talking: speaking and discussing
decisions.reason: The verb is used of reasoning and discussion (17:2, 18:4, 19:8). In 20:11 a plainer word for conversation is used.

decisions.choice: share the Lord's meal; the believers
decisions.reason: Readable explains breaking bread, following the meaning note, and says who "them" are.

records.heading: Eutychus at Troas

records.source: ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι·
records.gloss: There were then lamps many in the upper room where we were gathered.
pieces: There were plenty of lamps in the upstairs room where we had gathered.

L.8: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

R.8: Many oil lamps were burning in the upstairs room where we were meeting.

decisions.choice: many lamps: oil lamps, which gave off heat and smoke
alternatives: a detail with no bearing on the story
decisions.reason: Luke may mention them to explain the warm, close air that made the young man drowsy (20:9), or simply as a witness's memory. The text does not say why.

decisions.choice: upper room: a room on an upper floor
decisions.reason: As in 1:13 and 9:37. 20:9 shows it was on the third floor.

decisions.choice: oil lamps were burning
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of lamps they were.

records.source: καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος, καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον, κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός.
records.gloss: Sitting then a certain young man by name Eutychus on the window, being overcome by sleep deep, Paul discussing for longer, having been overcome by the sleep he fell from the third story down and was taken up dead.
pieces: A young man named Eutychus sat in the window opening. Paul's talk ran longer and longer, and Eutychus sank into a heavy sleep. Overcome by it, he fell from the third floor to the ground, and when they lifted him up he was dead.

L.9: And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, was being overcome by deep sleep as Paul talked still longer; overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.

R.9: A young man named Eutychus was sitting in an open window. Paul talked for a very long time, and Eutychus got sleepier and sleepier. At last he fell fast asleep and fell out of the window. He fell from the third floor all the way to the ground. When the people picked him up, he was dead.

decisions.choice: the window: an opening in the wall, with no glass
decisions.reason: Windows were open spaces, sometimes with shutters, wide enough to sit in.

decisions.choice: two steps: he was sinking into sleep, then sleep overcame him
decisions.reason: The first participle is present, of a process; the second is aorist, of the moment he was overcome.

decisions.choice: was picked up dead: he had died
decisions.reason: Luke says "dead", not "as if dead"; compare 14:19, where the crowd only supposed Paul was dead. 20:10 and 20:12 tell of him alive again.

decisions.choice: fell out of the window
decisions.reason: Readable says where he fell from, which the story implies.

records.source: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν· Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε, ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Having gone down then Paul fell upon him and having embraced said, Not be alarmed, the for life of him in him is.
pieces: Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and held him close. "Do not be upset," he said, "his life is in him."

L.10: But Paul went down, fell upon him, and taking [him] in his arms said, "Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him."

R.10: Paul went downstairs. He lay down on top of the young man and put his arms around him. Then he said to the people, "Do not be upset! He is alive."

decisions.choice: fell upon him and embraced him: as Elijah and Elisha did over dead boys
decisions.reason: Elijah stretched himself on the widow's son (1 Kings 17:21) and Elisha lay on the Shunammite's son (2 Kings 4:34), and both boys lived.

decisions.choice: do not be alarmed: stop the noisy distress of mourning
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the mourners' uproar in Mark 5:39. Its noun was the uproar of 20:1.

decisions.choice: his life is in him: he is alive now
decisions.reason: 20:9 says he was picked up dead and 20:12 that they brought him away alive. Paul's words announce that his life has returned, as Peter's do in 9:40.

decisions.choice: He is alive.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the phrase.

records.source: ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφ’ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς, οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν.
records.gloss: Having gone up then and having broken the bread and having eaten, for long and having talked until daybreak, thus he departed.
pieces: Then he went back upstairs, broke the bread and ate. He went on talking with them a long time, until dawn, and then he left.

L.11: And having gone up and broken the bread and eaten, and having talked a long while, until daybreak, so he departed.

R.11: Then Paul went back upstairs. He broke the bread and ate with them. He kept talking with them until the sun came up. Then he left.

decisions.choice: the bread: the bread they had gathered to break (20:7)
decisions.reason: The article points back to 20:7. The meal comes after midnight, once Eutychus is restored.

decisions.choice: talked: conversed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of ordinary conversation (Luke 24:14-15), unlike the discussion of 20:7 and 20:9.

decisions.choice: ate with them
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that it was a shared meal.

records.source: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα, καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως.
records.gloss: They brought then the boy living, and were comforted not moderately.
pieces: They led the boy away alive, and they were greatly comforted.

L.12: And they brought the boy [away] alive, and were comforted not a little.

R.12: The people took the young man home alive. They were very glad and greatly comforted.

decisions.choice: the boy: the young man of 20:9
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child, a youth or a servant. It refers to Eutychus, whom 20:9 calls a young man.

decisions.choice: not a little: very much
decisions.reason: Luke often says much by saying "not a little" (12:18, 19:23, 19:24).

decisions.choice: took home; very glad
decisions.reason: Readable supplies where they took him and what comfort meant to them here. "Home" is not in the Greek.

records.source: Ἡμεῖς δὲ προελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον, ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον, οὕτως γὰρ διατεταγμένος ἦν μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν.
records.gloss: We then having gone ahead to the ship set sail for Assos, from there being about to take on board the Paul; thus for having arranged he was, being about himself to go on foot.
pieces: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we meant to take Paul on board. He had arranged it this way, because he wanted to go there on foot.

L.13: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul on board there, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go on foot.

R.13: The rest of us went ahead to the ship and sailed to the town of Assos. We planned to pick Paul up there. Paul had planned it this way because he wanted to walk to Assos by land.

decisions.choice: Assos: a port south of Troas
decisions.reason: By road Assos was about twenty miles from Troas; by sea the ship had to round a cape.

decisions.choice: he himself was to go on foot: Paul alone went overland
decisions.reason: "Himself" sets Paul apart from the "we" who sailed. Luke does not give his reason.

decisions.choice: the rest of us; by land
decisions.reason: Readable makes the two routes clear.

records.heading: From Troas to Miletus

records.source: ὡς δὲ συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον, ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην, κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ἄντικρυς Χίου, τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς Σάμον, τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον·
records.gloss: When then he met with us at the Assos, having taken up him we came to Mitylene, \v 15 and from there having sailed away on the following [day] we arrived opposite Chios, then on the other [day] we crossed over to Samos, and on the next [day] we came to Miletus.
pieces: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
We sailed from there and the next day arrived off Chios. The day after that we crossed to Samos, and a day later we reached Miletus.

L.14: And when he met us at Assos, having taken him on board we came to Mitylene;
L.15: and sailing from there, on the following [day] we arrived opposite Chios, and on the next [day] we crossed over to Samos, and on the [day] after we came to Miletus.

R.14: Paul met us at Assos, and we took him on board. Then we sailed to Mitylene.
R.15: The next day we sailed from there and came to a place across the water from the island of Chios. The day after that we crossed over to the island of Samos. One day later we arrived at the city of Miletus.

decisions.choice: the places: Mitylene on the island of Lesbos, the islands of Chios and Samos, and the port of Miletus
decisions.reason: The ship worked its way south along the coast of Asia, stopping each night. Miletus lay about thirty miles south of Ephesus.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to Samos, and on the next day"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "and having stayed at Trogyllium" after Samos
decisions.reason: Trogyllium is a point on the mainland across from Samos. The words are in many later manuscripts and in Codex Bezae, but not in the early manuscripts the SBLGNT follows. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: opposite Chios: off the island, across the strait
decisions.reason: The word means facing; they anchored off the island, not at its harbor.

decisions.choice: the island of; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable says what each place is.

records.source: κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
records.gloss: Had decided for the Paul to sail past the Ephesus, so that not it might happen to him to spend time in the Asia; he was hurrying for, if possible it might be for him, the day of the Pentecost to be in Jerusalem.
pieces: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus so as not to lose time in the province of Asia. He was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if he could, by the day of Pentecost.

L.16: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem [on] the day of Pentecost.

R.16: Paul did not want to stop in Ephesus, because then he would have to spend too much time in the province of Asia. So he had decided to sail on past it. He was hurrying because he wanted to be in Jerusalem for the Festival of Pentecost, if he could.

decisions.choice: the day of Pentecost: the Festival of Weeks, fifty days after Passover
decisions.reason: Leviticus 23:15-21; Acts 2:1. Paul left Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread (20:6), so he had less than seven weeks to reach Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province whose chief city was Ephesus
decisions.reason: As in 16:6 and 19:10.

decisions.choice: sail past Ephesus: not call there, to save time
decisions.reason: Luke gives the reason himself: Paul was in a hurry. A visit would have kept him there.

decisions.choice: the Festival of Pentecost
decisions.reason: Readable says that Pentecost was a festival.

records.source: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
records.gloss: From then the Miletus having sent to Ephesus he summoned the elders of the church.
pieces: From Miletus he sent word to Ephesus and called the elders of the church to come to him.

L.17: And from Miletus, sending to Ephesus, he summoned the elders of the church.

R.17: While Paul was at Miletus, he sent a message to Ephesus. He asked the leaders of the church there, the elders, to come and meet him.

decisions.choice: elders: the leaders of a local church
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders in each church (14:23); the Jerusalem church had them too (11:30, 15:2). In 20:28 Paul calls these same men overseers.

decisions.choice: from Miletus to Ephesus: a journey of some days there and back
decisions.reason: Ephesus lay about thirty miles to the north, so the message and the elders' journey took time.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the church there, the elders
decisions.reason: Readable explains what elders are, and keeps the word.

records.heading: Paul speaks to the elders of Ephesus

records.source: ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφ’ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθ’ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην, δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
records.gloss: When then they came to him he said to them, You know, from [the] first day from which I set foot in the Asia, how with you the whole time I was, \v 19 serving the Lord with all humility and tears and trials the having happened to me by the plots of the Jews,
pieces: When they had come, he said to them, "From the first day I set foot in the province of Asia, you have seen what kind of life I led among you the whole time.
I worked as the Lord's servant, with all humility and with tears, enduring the trials that the plots of the Jews brought on me.

L.18: And when they had come to him, he said to them, "You know how I was with you the whole time from the first day that I set foot in Asia,
L.19: serving the Lord as a slave with all humility and tears and trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews;

R.18: When they came, Paul said to them, "You know what my life was like all the time I was with you, from the very first day I came to the province of Asia.
R.19: I served the Lord as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant. I was humble, and I often cried. I had many troubles because some of the Jews made plans against me.

decisions.choice: how I was with you: the way I lived among you
decisions.reason: Paul appeals to what they saw of his conduct, as in 1 Thessalonians 2:1-12.

decisions.choice: serving: the work of a slave for his master
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for slave. Paul calls himself a slave of Christ (Romans 1:1; Philippians 1:1).

decisions.choice: trials: hardships that tested him
decisions.reason: The word can mean either; here the trials come from the plots of others.

decisions.choice: the plots of the Jews: schemes against him by some of the Jews
decisions.reason: Acts 19:9 tells of opposition in the synagogue at Ephesus, and 20:3 of a plot in Greece; the plots at Ephesus are not described.

decisions.choice: worked as the Lord's servant / served the Lord as his servant
decisions.reason: The wording keeps the idea of serving as a slave that is in the verb. "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: I often cried; some of the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tears mean and that the plotters were some Jews, not all.

records.source: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατ’ οἴκους, διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν εἰς θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ πίστιν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: how nothing I held back of the profitable things of the not to declare to you and to teach you publicly and from house to house, \v 21 testifying solemnly both to Jews and to Greeks the toward God repentance and faith in the Lord of us Jesus.
pieces: You know how I held back nothing that was for your good, but made it known to you and taught you, in public and from house to house.
To Jews and Greeks alike I bore solemn witness about repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.

L.20: how I held back nothing of what was profitable, so as not to declare [it] to you and teach you publicly and from house to house,
L.21: solemnly testifying both to Jews and to Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.

R.20: You know that I told you everything that would help you. I did not hold anything back. I taught you in public places and in your homes.
R.21: I strongly urged both Jews and Greeks to turn away from their sins and come back to God, and to have faith in our Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: how: still depends on "you know" in 20:18
decisions.reason: The long sentence of 20:18-21 hangs on "you know".

decisions.choice: held back: shrank from, kept quiet out of fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw back or shrink. Paul uses it again in 20:27.

decisions.choice: Greeks: non-Jews, Gentiles
decisions.reason: In Acts "Jews and Greeks" means everyone (14:1, 18:4, 19:10).

decisions.choice: repentance: a change of mind and life, turning to God
decisions.reason: As in 2:38 and 3:19, repentance means turning back to God from sin.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "our Lord Jesus"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "our Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: The shorter reading is in several early manuscripts; many others add "Christ". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: You know how / You know that
decisions.reason: The English starts a new sentence after 20:19, so it repeats "you know" from 20:18.

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains repentance, following the meaning note.

records.source: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ δεδεμένος ἐγὼ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά μοι μὴ εἰδώς, πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν·
records.gloss: And now behold bound I in the spirit go to Jerusalem, the things in it going to meet me not knowing, \v 23 except that the Spirit the Holy in every city testifies solemnly to me saying that chains and afflictions me await.
pieces: And now, bound by the Spirit, I am on my way to Jerusalem. What I will meet there I do not know,
except that in one city after another the Holy Spirit bears witness to me that chains and hardships lie ahead of me.

L.22: And now, look, bound in the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will meet me there,
L.23: except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that chains and afflictions await me.

R.22: Now the Holy Spirit is leading me to Jerusalem, and I must go. I do not know what will happen to me there.
R.23: I only know this: in every city I visit, the Holy Spirit tells me that I will be put in chains and will suffer.

decisions.choice: bound in the Spirit: compelled by the Holy Spirit to go
alternatives: bound in my spirit: firmly resolved in his own mind
decisions.reason: The same phrase in 19:21 can mean either. In 20:23 and 21:4 it is the Holy Spirit who speaks about the journey, which favors the Holy Spirit here; but Paul's own resolve also fits.

decisions.choice: bound: under constraint; it also points ahead to the chains of 20:23
decisions.reason: He goes as one bound to obey, and he will soon be bound in fact (21:11, 21:33).

decisions.choice: in every city: in city after city along the way
decisions.reason: 21:4 and 21:10-11 show how the Spirit spoke through believers on the way.

decisions.choice: afflictions: troubles and distress
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pressures and persecutions believers suffer (14:22).

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit is leading me, and I must go
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning chosen above and explains "bound".

records.source: ἀλλ’ οὐδενὸς λόγου ποιοῦμαι τὴν ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: But of nothing account I make the life precious to myself, so as to finish the course of me and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly the gospel of the grace of the God.
pieces: But I set no value on my life, as if it were precious to me. All I want is to run my course to the end and carry out the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus: to bear full witness to the gospel of the grace of God.

L.24: But I do not account my life of any value [as] precious to myself, so that I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly to the gospel of the grace of God.

R.24: But my life does not matter to me. What matters is that I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me, like a runner who finishes the race. My work is to tell people the good news of God's grace, the kindness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows to people who do not deserve it.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the shorter reading
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "But I make account of none of these things, nor do I count my life precious to myself"
many manuscripts add "with joy" after "my course"
decisions.reason: The early manuscripts have the shorter, harder wording; the fuller forms smooth it out. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he counts his life worth nothing, compared with finishing his task
decisions.reason: The compressed Greek says that his own life is not what he holds dear; his aim is to complete what the Lord gave him.

decisions.choice: my course: the race a runner must finish
decisions.reason: Paul uses the picture of a race for his work (1 Corinthians 9:24; 2 Timothy 4:7).

decisions.choice: the gospel of the grace of God: the good news that God gives his favor freely
decisions.reason: Grace is God's undeserved kindness (15:11, 20:32).

decisions.choice: like a runner who finishes the race; the kindness he shows to people who do not deserve it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and the word grace, and keeps the word.

records.source: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν.
records.gloss: And now behold I know that no longer will see the face of me you all among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom.
pieces: And now I know this: you will not see my face again, not one of you among whom I have gone from place to place proclaiming the kingdom.

L.25: And now, look, I know that you all, among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom, will no longer see my face.

R.25: Now I know that none of you will see me again. I traveled among you and told you about God's kingdom, but you will not see me again.

decisions.choice: I know: Paul's firm conviction
decisions.reason: He does not say how he knows. The Spirit has warned him of chains (20:23), but not in these words.

decisions.choice: the kingdom: God's reign, which Paul proclaimed
decisions.reason: As in 19:8 and 28:31, where Paul proclaims the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the kingdom"
alternatives: some manuscripts read "the kingdom of God" or "the kingdom of Jesus"
decisions.reason: The short reading is in early manuscripts; the additions say whose kingdom it is. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable says whose kingdom, as 19:8 does.

records.source: διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων, οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Therefore I testify to you on the today day that clean I am from the blood of all; \v 27 not for I held back of the not to declare all the counsel of the God to you.
pieces: So on this day I solemnly tell you: I am free from guilt for anyone's blood.
I never drew back from making known to you God's whole plan.

L.26: Therefore I testify to you on this very day that I am clean from the blood of all,
L.27: for I did not hold back from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

R.26: So today I tell you this: if any of you are lost, it is not my fault.
R.27: I told you everything God wants you to know about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan.

decisions.choice: clean from the blood of all: free from guilt, like the watchman who gave warning
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 3:18-21 and 33:1-9 the watchman who warns the people is not guilty of their blood. Paul used the same picture in 18:6.

decisions.choice: counsel: God's purpose and plan
decisions.reason: As in 2:23, 4:28 and 13:36, the word is used of what God has willed and planned.

decisions.choice: this day: this last meeting
decisions.reason: Paul speaks as one who will not see them again (20:25).

decisions.choice: if any of you are lost, it is not my fault
alternatives: I am clean from the blood of all
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, following the meaning note.

records.source: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου.
records.gloss: Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, in which you the Spirit the Holy has placed overseers, to shepherd the church of the God, which he acquired through the blood of the own.
pieces: Be on your guard, for yourselves and for the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers to shepherd the church of God, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} won for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.

L.28: Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} acquired through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.

R.28: Be careful how you live, and watch over all the believers, who are like a flock of sheep. The Holy Spirit has put you in charge of them as overseers. Care for God's church as a shepherd cares for sheep. God paid for it with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the church of God"
alternatives: "the church of the Lord and God"
decisions.reason: Some of the oldest manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "of God". Others, among them Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Bezae, read "of the Lord", and many later ones combine the two. "Of God" with "his own blood" is the harder reading, which copyists may have softened; "of the Lord" is also early. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: through his own blood
alternatives: through the blood of his own [one], that is, his own Son
decisions.reason: The words can be read either way. Their order is the usual way of saying "his own blood", and the blood is the blood of Christ. But "his own" alone was used for a dear one, and Paul says God did not spare his own Son (Romans 8:32); read that way, the phrase names the Son. Some manuscripts change the order to "the own blood", which allows only the first reading.

decisions.choice: overseers: the elders of 20:17, who watch over the church
decisions.reason: Paul calls the same men elders (20:17) and overseers. The word means one who looks after others; later it became the title "bishop" (Philippians 1:1; 1 Timothy 3:1-2; Titus 1:5-7).

decisions.choice: flock and shepherd: God's people and those who care for them
decisions.reason: The picture comes from the Old Testament (Ezekiel 34) and from Jesus (John 10:11; 21:16); compare 1 Peter 5:2-3.

decisions.choice: acquired: won for himself, made his own at a cost
decisions.reason: The verb means to gain or secure for oneself (1 Timothy 3:13).

decisions.choice: be careful how you live; who are like a flock of sheep; as a shepherd cares for sheep
alternatives: take heed to yourselves and to the flock; to shepherd
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of flock and shepherd.

decisions.choice: paid for it
decisions.reason: Readable says that the church was gained at the cost of blood.

records.source: ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου, καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ἑαυτῶν·
records.gloss: I know that will come in after the departure of me wolves savage into you not sparing the flock, \v 30 and from you yourselves will rise up men speaking perverted things to draw away the disciples after themselves.
pieces: Once I have gone, I know, savage wolves will force their way in among you, with no mercy for the flock.
And from your own ranks {{gender:people|men}} will stand up and speak twisted things, to lure the disciples into following them.

L.29: I know that after my departure savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock,
L.30: and from among your own selves men will arise speaking perverted things, to draw away the disciples after them.

R.29: I know that after I leave, people will come among you who are like savage wolves. They will attack the flock and will not spare it.
R.30: Even some {{gender:people|men}} from your own group will begin to teach things that are twisted and false. They will try to get the followers of Jesus to follow them instead.

decisions.choice: savage wolves: people who will harm the church
decisions.reason: Jesus warned of false prophets who are wolves (Matthew 7:15) and of the wolf that scatters the flock (John 10:12).

decisions.choice: savage: fierce, dangerous
decisions.reason: The word means heavy, and so harsh or cruel.

decisions.choice: from among yourselves: from inside the church, even its leaders
decisions.reason: The second danger is set against the first: the wolves come in, these rise up from within.

decisions.choice: men: people from within the church
decisions.reason: The word is the one for men. Paul is speaking to the elders, who were men, but his point is that the danger will come from inside the church.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative; Literal keeps "men"
decisions.reason: The meaning note leaves open whether only men are meant.

decisions.choice: people ... who are like savage wolves; twisted and false
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and what twisted things are.

records.source: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε, μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον.
records.gloss: Therefore be watchful, remembering that three years night and day not I ceased with tears admonishing one each.
pieces: So be watchful, and remember: for three years I did not stop, night or day, admonishing each one of you with tears.

L.31: Therefore be watchful, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.

R.31: So be on guard! Remember that for three years I warned each one of you, day and night. I never stopped, and I often cried as I warned you.

decisions.choice: be watchful: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep awake, and so to be on guard (Mark 13:35-37).

decisions.choice: three years: his whole stay at Ephesus
decisions.reason: 19:8 and 19:10 give three months and two years, and more time followed (19:22). Parts of years were counted as whole years.

decisions.choice: admonishing: warning and correcting
decisions.reason: The word is used of warning someone for their good (1 Thessalonians 5:14).

records.source: καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ὑμᾶς τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, τῷ δυναμένῳ οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν.
records.gloss: And now I entrust you to the God and to the word of the grace of him, the [one] being able to build up and to give the inheritance among the having been sanctified all.
pieces: And now I place you in the care of God and of the message of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace. That message has power to build you up and to give you your share among all who have been made holy.

L.32: And now I entrust you to God and to the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, which is able to build [you] up and to give [you] the inheritance among all those who have been sanctified.

R.32: Now I am putting you into God's care, and I trust you to the message of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace. This message can make you strong. It can give you what God has promised to all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people.

decisions.choice: which is able: the word of his grace
decisions.reason: The words "being able" follow "the word" most closely, and God's word builds up (compare James 1:21). But they could also go back to God, as in Romans 16:25 and Jude 24.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to God"
decisions.reason: Both readings are early. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share in what God gives his people
decisions.reason: As Israel received a share of the land, believers have a share among God's people (26:18; Colossians 1:12).

decisions.choice: sanctified: set apart for God, made holy
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 26:18.

decisions.choice: what God has promised to all his holy people
alternatives: the inheritance among all who are sanctified
decisions.reason: Readable explains inheritance and sanctified in plain words.

records.source: ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα·
records.gloss: Silver or gold or clothing of no one I coveted.
pieces: I never set my heart on anyone's silver or gold or clothing.

L.33: I coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing.

R.33: I never wanted anyone's money or fine clothes.

decisions.choice: silver, gold, clothing: the forms wealth took
decisions.reason: Fine clothing was a store of wealth (Joshua 7:21; James 5:2).

decisions.choice: an echo of Samuel's farewell
decisions.reason: Samuel, leaving his office, asked whose ox or donkey he had taken (1 Samuel 12:3). The likeness is general.

decisions.choice: money or fine clothes
decisions.reason: Readable says what silver and gold meant: money.

records.source: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετ’ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.
records.gloss: Yourselves you know that to the needs of me and to those being with me served the hands these.
pieces: You know yourselves that I provided for my own needs, and for those who were with me, with these hands.

L.34: You yourselves know that these hands served my needs and [those of] the ones who were with me.

R.34: You know that I worked with my own hands to earn what I needed. I also earned what the people with me needed.

decisions.choice: these hands: Paul's own work as a tentmaker
decisions.reason: Paul worked at his trade in Corinth (18:3), and speaks of it in 1 Corinthians 4:12 and 1 Thessalonians 2:9. "These" suggests he showed them his hands.

decisions.choice: those with me: his fellow workers
decisions.reason: Paul's companions, such as those named in 20:4 and 19:22.

decisions.choice: I provided ... with these hands
decisions.reason: Balanced makes Paul the subject and keeps "these hands" to the end for emphasis.

records.source: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων, μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν.
records.gloss: All things I showed you that thus laboring it is necessary to help the being weak, to remember and the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, Blessed it is more to give than to receive.
pieces: In every way I set you an example: by working hard like this we must come to the aid of the weak, and keep in mind the words of the Lord Jesus, how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

L.35: In all things I showed you that by laboring like this we must help the weak, and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

R.35: In all I did, I showed you that we must work hard like this and help people who are weak or in need. We must remember what the Lord Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} said: 'Giving brings more blessing than receiving.'"

decisions.choice: we must: a duty that binds Paul and his hearers alike
decisions.reason: The verb names no subject; it states what is necessary for everyone in the elders' place.

decisions.choice: the weak: those in need, whether poor or sick
decisions.reason: With working hard and giving, the context points to people who cannot provide for themselves.

decisions.choice: a saying of Jesus not recorded in the Gospels
decisions.reason: The words are not found in the four Gospels, though Jesus taught similar things (Luke 6:38, 14:12-14). Paul passes it on as words of Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: blessed: happy, favored by God
decisions.reason: The word of the Beatitudes (Luke 6:20-22).

decisions.choice: Giving brings more blessing than receiving.
alternatives: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the saying in plainer words.

decisions.choice: weak or in need
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning note.

records.source: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο.
records.gloss: And these things having said, having placed the knees of him with all them he prayed.
pieces: After saying this, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

L.36: And having said these things, he knelt down with them all and prayed.

R.36: After Paul said these things, he got down on his knees and prayed with all of them.

decisions.choice: knelt: a posture of earnest prayer
decisions.reason: Standing was the usual posture for prayer; kneeling marks deep need (7:60, 9:40, 21:5; Luke 22:41).

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker at the end of the speech.

records.heading: Farewell at Miletus

records.source: ἱκανὸς δὲ κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο πάντων, καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν, ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν.
records.gloss: Much then weeping there was of all, and having fallen on the neck of the Paul they were kissing him, \v 38 grieving most at the word which he had spoken, that no longer they are going the face of him to see.
pieces: They all wept freely. They threw their arms around Paul and kissed him again and again.
Above all, they were pained by what he had said, that they would not see his face any more.

L.37: And there was much weeping among them all, and falling on Paul's neck, they kissed him again and again,
L.38: grieving most of all over the word that he had spoken, that they were no longer going to see his face.

R.37: Everyone cried. They hugged Paul and kissed him.
R.38: They were very sad, most of all because he had said that they would never see him again.

decisions.choice: fell on his neck and kissed him: a farewell embrace
decisions.reason: As when the father met the lost son (Luke 15:20) and Joseph met his brothers (Genesis 45:14-15).

decisions.choice: kissed: again and again
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures repeated action.

decisions.choice: the word: his statement in 20:25
decisions.reason: They repeat what he said in 20:25.

decisions.choice: hugged
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for the gesture.

records.source: προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον.
records.gloss: They were accompanying then him to the ship.
pieces: Then they went with him down to the ship.

L.38: And they accompanied him to the ship.

R.38: Then they walked with him to the ship.

decisions.choice: accompanied: escorted him on his way
decisions.reason: The verb is used of seeing travelers off (15:3, 21:5).
